name: LPW Championship
epitaph: The top belt of Legend Pro Wrestling's 2002 relaunch, vacant for two years after the first run closed and decided by a single-elimination tournament. Jake MacKenna, billed as a rookie sensation, won it at Clash of the Champions on 13 April 2002 after Devastator wrecked Kobra Khan in the final. Andrew Dixon held it by 3 May, and he vacated it on 5 May, leaving the belt without a champion.

name: LPW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Vacant when Legend Pro Wrestling reopened in March 2002 and filled within two weeks: the Shadowlords won it on 12 March, the Oriental Assassins took it from them on 9 April after an unseen figure's darts, and the Puerto Rican Slayers won it from the Assassins on 13 April in a Final Confrontation superfight that sent the Assassins out of the promotion. The Slayers still held it on 3 May 2002.

name: LPW Lightweight Championship
epitaph: A five-man tournament that began on 22 March 2002 was meant to crown the first Lightweight champion of Legend Pro Wrestling's relaunch. Rock And Roll Rebel was champion by 9 April, when he kept the belt against Dragon Ninja after both men's finishers landed at once, and Dead Skull held it by 3 May.

name: LPW National Championship
epitaph: Vacant through Legend Pro Wrestling's 2002 relaunch until Wesley Potter beat Johnny Ziro for it at Clash of the Champions on 13 April 2002, helped by the Assassin, who pulled the referee from the ring and clubbed Ziro. Its name follows its champion's nationality, so Potter's reign was billed as the United States National title. He held it on the last card.

name: LPW Superfight Championship
epitaph: Vacant when Legend Pro Wrestling reopened in March 2002 and decided in a career-ending steel cage match on 15 March, when Kobra Khan threw Hurricane Wild Child through the cage wall and ended his career in the promotion. Khan kept the belt past Devastator on 19 April after Andrew Dixon and Paul Setzer shocked Devastator with a defibrillator, and Dead Skull carried it by 3 May.

name: Undisputed Universal Championship
epitaph: The Undisputed Universal title was defended by Adam Simon on 3 May 2002 in a best-of-three-falls superfight with Zodiac, who beat him two falls to one with the Big Bang off the top rope onto the commentary table after twelve years away from the ring.
